docs.text: Hardware-based field-oriented control HardFOC ¶ Open firmware for ESP32 motor and valve controller boards. Motor commutation runs on dedicated FOC driver chips, such as the TMC9660, instead of in MCU software; the firmware around them is C++ on ESP-IDF and FreeRTOS, split into portable chip drivers, a shared core, board HALs and one application per board. Get started All repositories HardFOC on GitHub Start with a board, or a chip ¶ Vortex V1 motor controller ESP32-C6 with a TMC9660 smart gate driver running FOC on chip, an AS5047U magnetic encoder and CAN (CANopen). Flux V1 valve controller ESP32-S3 with on/off and proportional solenoid channels on a TLE92466ED and a MAX22200. A chip driver on your own MCU Every hf-*-driver is hardware-agnostic C++: no platform code, one small bus adapter, ESP32 examples. How the code is layered ¶ Four layers, each a set of repositories Figure description and sources From bottom to top, each layer builds on the one below it as a Git submodule pinned to a commit or tag. Chip drivers are hardware-agnostic C++ libraries with no platform code; each one needs only a small bus adapter. hf-core gathers them with the peripheral interface wrap, the pin configuration and the utility libraries (RTOS wrappers, general helpers, CANopen). A board HAL builds one object per board from hf-core, with one manager per board function. A product is the application firmware for one board, on top of its HAL. Drawn from: mkdocs.yml ; figure module docs/diagrams/figures/hardfoc-layers.py . Each box is one or more repositories; each arrow is a Git submodule pinned to a commit or tag. The architecture page shows the repositories in each layer. Documentation ¶ Every repository with a documentation site publishes it at https://hardfoc.github.io/<repository>/ , versioned: latest/ is the newest release (or the default branch until the first release), and older versions stay available. The repository catalogue links each one, with its topics and latest release. Repositories Every public repository, searchable by name, description and topic. Architecture Drivers, core, HALs and products, and how they are pinned together. Contribute How to report a problem, propose a change, and report a vulnerability privately.

docs.text:
Architecture ¶ How HardFOC firmware is split into repositories, and how the layers are pinned together. Four layers, each a set of repositories Figure description and sources From bottom to top, each layer builds on the one below it as a Git submodule pinned to a commit or tag. Chip drivers are hardware-agnostic C++ libraries with no platform code; each one needs only a small bus adapter. hf-core gathers them with the peripheral interface wrap, the pin configuration and the utility libraries (RTOS wrappers, general helpers, CANopen). A board HAL builds one object per board from hf-core, with one manager per board function. A product is the application firmware for one board, on top of its HAL. Drawn from: mkdocs.yml ; figure module docs/diagrams/figures/hardfoc-layers.py . Layers ¶ Layer Repositories Depends on Contains Products hardfoc-vortex-v1 , hardfoc-flux-v1 One board HAL The application: tasks, protocols (CANopen on Vortex), faults; ESP-IDF only in its start-up code Board HALs hf-hal-vortex-v1 , hf-hal-flux-v1 hf-core One facade per board, one manager per board function, and the platform bind: the only code that names the MCU Core hf-core , gathering hf-core-drivers and hf-core-utils Drivers, interface wrap, utilities One handler per chip (locking, start-up, error mapping), the logger, CANopen integration Interface wrap hf-internal-interface-wrap , hf-pincfg The MCU vendor SDK, only inside each family's implementation Platform-free peripheral base classes (GPIO, ADC, I2C, SPI, UART, CAN, PWM, NVS, timers, temperature, logging) with implementations for ESP32 (ESP-IDF), STM32 (STM32 HAL) and the host; header-only per-board pin maps Utilities hf-utils-general , hf-utils-canopen , hf-utils-rtos-wrap None; rtos-wrap uses the selected RTOS General helpers and CANopen frame builders, platform-free, in headers and sources; RTOS wrappers with FreeRTOS, CMSIS-RTOS2, ThreadX and no-RTOS backends Chip drivers hf-*-driver Nothing Platform-free C++20 templates over a small communication interface you implement; MCU-bound drivers such as hf-ws2812-rmt-driver say so The repository catalogue lists every repository in each layer, with its documentation. The stack contract ¶ What each layer promises, what it may include, and the rules for errors, threads, time and naming are in the HardFOC engineering standard : Topic Page The layers and their allowed includes Layers One error model across the stack Errors Locks, clocks, delays and the 1 kHz tick Threading and timing Contracts per layer Driver , library , handler , board HAL , product Why it is this way Architecture decision records Submodules, not packages ¶ Each arrow in the figure is a Git submodule pinned to a commit or tag: flowchart LR drv["Chip drivers
hf-*-driver"] --> cd["hf-core-drivers"] iw["hf-internal-interface-wrap
hf-pincfg"] --> cd ut["hf-utils-general
hf-utils-rtos-wrap
hf-utils-canopen"] --> cu["hf-core-utils"] cd --> core["hf-core"] cu --> core core --> hal["Board HALs"] hal --> prod["Products"] A product therefore builds exactly the commits it pins, all the way down. Moving a layer forward is a pull request that updates one submodule pointer and passes that repository's CI. Shared tooling ¶ Repository Provides hf-general-ci-tools Reusable workflows (lint, analysis, host builds, the CI gate, releases) and the documentation platform this site is built with hf-espidf-ci-tools ESP-IDF builds of examples and firmware, releases with artifacts hf-espidf-project-tools Build and flash scripts for ESP-IDF example projects Next: Get started .

docs.text: Contribute ¶ How to report a problem, propose a change and report a vulnerability, for every HardFOC repository. Report a problem or ask a question ¶ Open an issue in the repository closest to the problem: the driver for a chip, the HAL for a board, the product for the application. If you cannot tell, open it in the product and say what you saw. Propose a change ¶ Step Where Read the rules for branches, commits, pull requests and the CI gate CONTRIBUTING.md Follow the engineering standard for code, layering, naming, releases and AI agents HardFOC engineering standard Follow the code of conduct CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md Write documentation to the shared standard Documentation style guide Add CI to a repository CI quickstart A repository with its own CONTRIBUTING.md follows that file instead. Report a vulnerability ¶ Never in public Do not open a public issue, pull request or discussion for a suspected vulnerability. Report it privately with a GitHub security advisory: in the affected repository, Security > Advisories > Report a vulnerability . The security policy says what to include and what is in scope. This site ¶ The portal is hardfoc/hardfoc.github.io . The repository list is built from the GitHub API and the organisation's repository record each time the site is published; to change a description or topics, change org/org-metadata.json in hardfoc/.github .

docs.text: Figures ¶ Every figure on this site is drawn by a Python module from facts extracted from the code, so it is rebuilt, not redrawn, when the code changes. CI runs hardfoc-docs figures --check and fails when a committed figure no longer matches the code. Each figure below lists the files it is drawn from. Four layers, each a set of repositories ¶ Four layers, each a set of repositories Figure description and sources From bottom to top, each layer builds on the one below it as a Git submodule pinned to a commit or tag. Chip drivers are hardware-agnostic C++ libraries with no platform code; each one needs only a small bus adapter. hf-core gathers them with the peripheral interface wrap, the pin configuration and the utility libraries (RTOS wrappers, general helpers, CANopen). A board HAL builds one object per board from hf-core, with one manager per board function. A product is the application firmware for one board, on top of its HAL. docs.text: A chip driver on your MCU ¶ Use one HardFOC chip driver in your own firmware, on any MCU, without the rest of HardFOC. Every hf-*-driver repository is a C++ library with no platform code. The driver is a class template over a small communication interface: you write one class that moves bytes over the bus (SPI, I2C or UART) and toggles the chip's control pins, and the driver does the rest. Each one ships ESP32 examples that build in CI. Path ¶ Find the chip in the catalogue (filter by bus: spi , i2c , uart ). Read its quickstart : wiring, the port class and a short example, compiled in CI. For example, the TMC9660 quickstart . Add it as a submodule and link its CMake target, or add it as an ESP-IDF component. Write the port for your MCU, following the driver's porting page, and run the example. What every driver has ¶ Page What it covers Quickstart Wiring, the port, a short example, "if it does not work" Hardware Pins, bus settings and timing, power, errata Porting The interface methods and their contracts API guide and reference Task-oriented guide, and Doxygen under api/ Examples The ESP32 examples and what each one shows

docs.text: Flux V1 valve controller ¶ From a new Flux V1 board to its examples running, and where to read next. Valve controller board Flux V1 HardFOC MCU ESP32-S3 Solenoid drivers TLE92466ED (six low-side channels), MAX22200 (eight channels) Valves On/off and proportional solenoid channels Firmware ESP-IDF 5.5, FreeRTOS, C++ Path ¶ Bring the board up with the HAL. The HAL quickstart installs ESP-IDF, builds an example and reads its log. Check the hardware. The pin map and the bring-up guide . Drive the valves. The ValveManager page and the examples. The product firmware, hardfoc-flux-v1 , is a private repository. Its documentation is built in CI as an artifact for people with access, and is not published here. Documentation ¶ Site What it covers hf-hal-flux-v1 The board: hardware, pin map, managers (valves, ADC, GPIO, LEDs, temperature, NVS, comms), examples hf-tle92466ed-driver The six-channel solenoid driver hf-max22200-driver The eight-channel solenoid driver hf-core The shared core the HAL is built on
